title: coord keeps an operation job as the key job/ID with a state table of its own, and every move posts a job event
goal: coord.py transition accepts a key job/ID with a table of its own (none to queued; queued to running or cancelled; running to waiting-lock, waiting-merge, succeeded, failed, refused, cancelled or lost; waiting-lock and waiting-merge back to running or on to cancelled; lost to queued or failed; succeeded, failed, refused and cancelled move nowhere), posts a job event of job, state, op, item, exit, step, by and attempt on every move, and a move the table refuses exits 1 naming the state the key holds, while an unknown state exits 2; coord.py wait --kind job returns on such an event; the table of run/ITEM keys is unchanged (queued is no run state, exit 2)

run: import json,subprocess,sys,tempfile,os; s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); co=lambda *a: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",s,*a],capture_output=True,text=True); t=lambda k,to,*f: co("transition",k,"--to",to,*f).returncode; k="job/JB-aaaaaaaa"; assert t(k,"queued")==0 and t(k,"running")==0; assert t(k,"queued")==1; assert t(k,"succeeded","--field","exit=0")==0; assert t(k,"running")==1; assert t(k,"bogus")==2; assert t("run/ST-aaaaaaaa","queued")==2; ev=json.loads(co("wait","--since","0","--timeout","0","--kind","job").stdout)["events"]; assert [e["fields"]["state"] for e in ev]==["queued","running","succeeded"], ev
